Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority

FAQs

1.What are State Legal Services AuthoriƟes? What are their roles and responsibiliƟes?

A State Legal Services Authority (SLSA) is consƟtuted for every State/Union Territory
under SecƟon 6 of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987. The SLSA is headed by the Chief
JusƟce of the High Court of the respecƟve State, as its Patron-in-Chief. SLSAs give eﬀect to
the policy and direcƟons of NALSA, and are assigned the following funcƟons under SecƟon 7
of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987:

1. Give legal service to persons who saƟsfy the criteria laid down under SecƟon 12 of
the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987;

2. Conduct Lok Adalats, including Lok Adalats for High Court cases;

3. Undertake prevenƟve and strategic legal aid programmes; and

4. Perform such other funcƟons as the State Authority may, in consultaƟon with NALSA,
ﬁx by RegulaƟons.

2.What is District Legal Services AuthoriƟes and Taluk Legal Services CommiƩees? What
are their roles and responsibiliƟes?

SecƟon 9 of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987, provides for the consƟtuƟon of
the District Legal Services AuthoriƟes (DLSAs) by the State Government, in consultaƟon with
the Chief JusƟce of the High Court, for every District in the State, to exercise the powers and
perform the funcƟons conferred on, or assigned to, the DLSA under SecƟons 10 and 11 of
the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987. The DLSA is headed by the District & Sessions Judge
of the respecƟve district as the Chairman, DLSA.

Similarly, SecƟon 11A of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987, provides for the
consƟtuƟon of the Taluka Legal Services CommiƩees (TLSC) by the State Authority for each
Taluka or mandal or for a group of Talukas or mandals, to exercise the powers and perform
the funcƟons conferred on, or assigned to them, under SecƟon 11B of the Legal Services
AuthoriƟes Act, 1987. The TLSC is headed by the senior Civil Judge operaƟng within its
jurisdicƟon as the ex-oﬃcio Chairman.

As per SecƟons 10 and 11 of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987, it shall be the duty
of every DLSA to perform such of the funcƟons of the State Authority in the District as may
be delegated to it from Ɵme to Ɵme by the State Authority. The DLSA may perform all or any
of the following funcƟons, namely:

1. Coordinate the acƟviƟes of the TLSC and other legal services in the District;

2. Organize Lok Adalats within the District;

The DLSAs are expected to act in coordinaƟon with other agencies and be subject to
direcƟons given by the NALSA, for promoƟng the cause of legal services to the poor.

As per SecƟon 11B of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987, it shall be the duty of every

1. Co-ordinate the acƟviƟes of legal services in the Taluka;

2. Organize Lok Adalats within the Taluka; and

3. Perform such other funcƟons as the DLSA may assign to it.

3.What is High Court Legal Services CommiƩees? What are their roles and
responsibiliƟes?

SecƟon 8A of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987, provides that the SLSA shall
consƟtute a CommiƩee to be called the High Court Legal Services CommiƩee (HCLSC) for
every High Court, for the purpose of exercising such powers and performing such funcƟons
as may be determined by RegulaƟons made by the State Authority. It is headed by a siƫng
Judge of the concerned High Court, as the Chairman. HCLSCs have been established to
provide free and competent legal services to weaker secƟons of the society who wish to ﬁle
or defend a case in the concerned High Court of a State.

4.What is Supreme Court Legal Services CommiƩee? What are its roles and
responsibiliƟes?
The Supreme Court Legal Services CommiƩee (SCLSC) is consƟtuted under SecƟon 3A of
the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987, to provide free and competent legal services to
those who fall within the purview of SecƟon 12 of the Legal Services AuthoriƟes Act, 1987,
in cases that fall under the jurisdicƟon of the Supreme Court of India.

5.What are Legal Services? What included in free legal aid provided by the Legal Services
InsƟtuƟons? What is the nature of free Legal Services?

According to SecƟon 2(c) of the Act, “legal services” includes any service in the conduct
of any case or other legal proceeding before any court or other authority or tribunal and the
giving of advice on any legal maƩer. It includes free legal services in civil and criminal
maƩers for those poor and marginalized people who cannot aﬀord the services of a lawyer
for the conduct of a case or a legal proceeding in any Court, Tribunal or Authority. Provision
of free legal aid may include:

1. RepresentaƟon by an Advocate in legal proceedings;

2. Payment of process fees, expenses of witnesses and all other charges (charges such
as court fees, stamp duty etc.) payable or incurred in connecƟon with any legal
proceedings in appropriate cases (provided that Court Fees will be payable only aŌer

6. How is free legal aid diﬀerent from free legal advice and assistance?

Legal aid is the provision of legal representaƟon to a person in the District Courts, High
Courts and Supreme Court or tribunals, by a lawyer assigned by the Legal Service Authority
concerned.

Legal Advice and Assistance is the provision of advice on general areas of law as
governed by the laws of India by the lawyers employed with the Legal Services InsƟtuƟon
concerned. For e.g. if a person has to ﬁle a case in court, he would be provided legal aid (in
form of assignment of a Legal Services Advocate). However, if he only needs some help in
draŌing a legal noƟce to be sent prior to ﬁling of a complaint under SecƟon 138 of the
NegoƟable Instruments Act 1881, he would get legal consultaƟon/ advice regarding the
same. A person who does not come under the purview of SecƟon 12 of Legal Services
AuthoriƟes Act, 1987, to be eligible for free legal aid, can sƟll avail legal advice and
assistance from the Legal Services InsƟtuƟons.
